Harbour bridge reopens after two years of repairs

By Mara Lindqvist

The harbour bridge, closed since the storm two winters ago, reopened to traffic on Monday morning, with cyclists, buses and a long line of delivery vans crossing before seven o'clock.

Engineers replaced the steel cables, rebuilt both approach ramps and added a separate lane for bicycles, which the council says will make the crossing safer for everyone, especially children on their way to school.

The repairs cost more than first planned, partly because corrosion inside the north tower was worse than surveys had shown, and partly because steel prices rose sharply during the second year of work.

What changes for drivers

Drivers will pay the same toll as before, but the council has promised a review in the spring, after residents complained that the toll falls hardest on people who commute from the island every day.

Buses will return to their old routes from next week, the transport authority said, and the temporary ferry, which carried more than a million passengers during the closure, will stop running at the end of the month.

Shop owners near the southern ramp, who say they lost customers during the closure, welcomed the news, although several said it would take months for trade to recover fully.
